blocks.content: The executive power of the Union shall be vested in the President and shall be exercised by him either directly or through officers subordinate to him in accordance with this Constitution.

rows: Can pardon death sentences and court-martial (Art 72)
Cannot pardon death sentences or court-martial (Art 161)
Supreme Commander of Armed Forces; handles treaties

items: Article 123 (Ordinance power of President) vs Article 213 (Ordinance power of Governor) is frequently tested in Polity exams.
President's pardoning power under Article 72 differs from Governor's under Article 161 regarding death sentences and court martial.
Money Bills require prior recommendation of the President before introduction in Lok Sabha.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: All executive actions of the Government of India are formally taken in the name of the President.
The President can promulgate ordinances under Article 123 only when both Houses of Parliament are not in session.
Pardoning power under Article 72 extends to punishments by Court Martial and death sentences.
The President summons or prorogues Parliament and can dissolve the Lok Sabha.
